inspectedLocal.caption: 42nd St facade of New York City's Grand Central Terminal in 2019. taken as part of a scheduled photoshoot with three other Wikipedians on January 7, 2019.
inspectedLocal.inspection: 2019 full6000x4000 original inspected, with focused native crop of Glory of Commerce/clock: three huge arch windows, paired fluted monumental columns, smaller oval garlanded windows, attic/cornice/dentils, side cartouches, green copper roof and lower granite storefront level. Integral central Mercury, winged/eagle forms, seated Hercules/Minerva, coloured Roman-numeral clock and sculpted pediment are important. Neighbouring glass towers and temporary flags/street furniture excluded.

sources.inspection: Primary NYC LPC1967 exterior designation read: monumental Beaux-Arts building, large glazed windows, massive columns, oval surrounds and clock. Supports features, not a measured elevation.

Primary NPS1976 nomination read: street-level granite/upper limestone, three arched front windows, four main entrance routes, Hercules/Minerva/Mercury facade group. Historical above-grade building dimensions and nominated property boundary are different:301ft building width vs394.4ft property frontage, and673ft historical building length vs340.4ft nominated front-site depth. Do not blindly use OSM outline as a solid facade or reconstruct northern tower/underground tracks.

Aerial inspected: distinct front green standing-seam roof, own side-wing green roofs, central broad light roof panels with low ridges, front own mechanical well and northern MetLife interface. Curved vehicular viaduct wraps south/sides and lies outside terminal facade. Current ground/roof parallax is not a measured footprint. Central roof slab dimensions/profile remain to reconcile.
Operator text read: describes viaduct as a separate illuminated structure and identifies family oak/acorn architectural ornament. No interior clock/ceiling is within exterior model scope.

Official NYC photogrammetric footprint BIN1035381/doitt49507, named Grand Central Terminal, actual polygon inspected. Rotated own envelope91.584m wide x87.720m deep, southern projecting wall85.807m wide. Agrees primary historical301ft width91.745m; distinguishes own wall from OSM121x104m viaduct/property envelope. height_roof150.4ft=45.84192m is contextual max, not a roof slab elevation. Ground_elevation54ft is coarse attribute, not a flattening datum.

Rendered whole operator directory plan inspected. Vanderbilt Hall south of main concourse, side routes and northern MetLife interface. Track areas/passages beyond current above-grade terminal are excluded.
Rendered whole lower-concourse plan inspected. Explicit128ft scale bar; lower track loop and adjacent Hyatt separate from above-grade exterior. Not traced as exterior wall plan.

Project restoration architect record read: exterior limestone/granite base, copper and flat roofs, brick at hidden locations, bronze entrances and large painted-metal double windows, Vanderbilt bronze figure and integral limestone sculpture/clock.

Rendered full2010 operator north-south/east-west sections inspected. Waiting-room/front facade, lower inner area-way, raised shallow pitched main-concourse attic over internal vault, three great arched side windows with flanking lower rectangular wings, MetLife separate at north. Exterior roof profile follows section plus current aerial; exact elevations remain proportional estimates, not scaled construction tracing.

Northern MetLife/Hyatt/Graybar/One Vanderbilt buildings, viaduct/bridge/roads, underground train shed/tracks/interiors, temporary flags/shop signs/awnings, street furniture and surrounding sidewalks excluded.
